note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 10(1), 12, PAN 1, 4, 8, Decree-Law No. 3 of 22 February 2008 Title XIII; A06b Const 10(1), 12, PAN 1, 4, 8, Decree-Law No. 3 of 22 February 2008 Title XIII; L05 Const 13): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another (loss applies only to naturalised citizens, not modelled). Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Panama, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Panama for a continuous period of 5 years (time spent during minority is fully counted). ... Oath of renunciation of citizenship of another country required (proof of renunciation is not required). ... Person is a citizen by naturalisation and acquires citizenship of another country.
